items.title: Per uno scienziato forense Jeffrey Epstein è stato ucciso, non si è suicidato
items.summary: Lo rivelano le foto, 'le lesioni non trovano riscontro nel suicidio'
items.content: Le foto dell'autopsia di Jeffrey Epstein mostrano che è stato ucciso. Lo ha detto Michael Freeman, scienziato forense esperto di omicidi, che ha avuto accesso al fascicolo relativo alla morte del finanziere. Secondo quanto riporta il New York Times, Freeman ha esposto la sua tesi a Middle Temple, associazione di legali di Londra, osservando come le ferite riportate da Epstein possono essere spiegate come conseguenza di uno strangolamento a scopo di omicidio. Le lesioni sul corpo del finanziere, inoltre, sarebbero la prova di una colluttazione. "La tipologia, la distribuzione e la molteplicità delle lesioni non trovano riscontro" in un suicidio, ha messo in evidenza.

items.title: Vance says he will decide 'sometime next year' about 2028 US presidential run
items.summary: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".
items.content:
US Vice-President JD Vance has said he will make a decision "sometime next year" about whether or not he will run for president in 2028.

In an interview with Fox News, Vance would not provide a timeline on making a determination, but signaled he is not in a hurry to make up his mind.

"I haven't made a decision. We'll figure it out sometime next year," Vance said. When pressed by host Laura Ingraham, he added: "When I make a decision, I'll be all in on whatever that decision is."

The comments came amid growing interest in Vance's next moves in the weeks since voters handed both President Donald Trump and Republicans a resounding defeat in the midterm elections.

People in Vance's orbit who have spoken to the BBC said the November elections did not change the timeline around his decision-making process for 2028. He is expected to run but allies believe he could wait several months to make a final decision.

Speculation about Vance's White House aspirations began the moment President Trump selected him as his 2024 running mate. The pick positioned Vance, who entered the White House as one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, as the most likely heir to Trump's Make America Great Again (Maga) movement.

But while serving in office, Vance has carefully avoided discussing his own political ambitions.

He kept that up during the midterms, when supporters frequently interrupted his campaign speeches to urge him to run in 2028. Vance's stock response was that Republicans needed to focus on the election at hand in November.

But with the midterms in the rearview mirror, and Republicans eager to move on from their 2026 drubbing, the next election at hand is now the 2028 presidential race.

Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war

The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?

Vance would likely jump to the top of the Republican primary field whenever he launches his bid, should he choose to run. But the contest is expected to be a competitive process with a large field of candidates.

Numerous other high-profile Republicans are rumoured to be interested in running or have said publicly that they are mulling a White House bid.

The list includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, outgoing Florida Governor and 2024 hopeful Ron DeSantis, and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, among others.

Trump has praised Vance and Rubio on several occasions, while also insisting that he is not sure who he will endorse in 2028 - or if he will weigh in at all.

The president's endorsement would be influential with the Maga base. But the midterms revealed widespread frustration with many of his second-term policies, complicating the path forward for potential candidates like Vance who are tied to Trump's agenda.

Vance blamed the midterm results on the war with Iran in a post-election social media post. In it, he also mapped out a plan for winning back Republican voters, which included ending the war and focusing on the economy.

The message was widely seen as a first step by Vance to distance himself from Trump ahead of a 2028 run.

In the Fox News interview, Vance reiterated his view that the war came with a "political cost", but said it has not damaged his relationship with Trump.

"There's no daylight" on the Iran war between Trump and senior administration officials including himself, Vance said.

He added that Trump would not let the conflict become a "forever war" and said the administration would not let the war, which was launched by the US and Israel in February 2026, even become "a two-year commitment".

Vance also discussed the nationwide air traffic outrage last week , which brought air travel across the US to a standstill for several hours. The vice-president called on lawmakers to fix the issue in the final weeks of the current congressional session.

He also touched on the scandal engulfing Nvidia , its former CEO Jensen Huang and its implications for US-China relations. Vance said there was still no "clarity" about the accuracy of reports that a woman with whom Huang reportedly had an affair with was indeed a Chinese spy.

"There is a lack of clarity about it. I don't know and [Trump] doesn't know whether this woman was a spy or not," Vance said.

Four things we learned from midterms about 2028 White House race

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex boss
items.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.content:
Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for the company's co-founder Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, supported the effort.

Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, joining a list of supporters including SpaceX's Elon Musk who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in reinstating him after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs , including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

The same day, the White House also said it will further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance.

Since Huang's departure, more than 175,000 people have signed an open letter calling for the board to reinstate the tech billionaire while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

Major tech bosses, including Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive.

They expressed concerns the firm's co-founder "was removed without meaningful due process".

Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of the affair but resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times , external , though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".

Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which have been allegedly used as a way for Chinese firms to gain access to advanced chips to train AI models.

The move comes ahead of a meeting this week between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping , whose countries are locked in a race to lead AI development.

The interim rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to prevent them from being illegally diverted to China.

The measure is designed to ensure existing restrictions on sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Department of Commerce said.

Huang has been a vocal advocate for easing chip export restrictions on China, arguing that broad access to global markets is crucial for the competitiveness of the US.

He said in 2025 that the market for AI chips in China would eventually reach $50bn - a sum Huang said "is like Boeing - not a plane - the entire company".

In 2025, Nvidia won an approval to sell some advanced AI chips in China after Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington.

How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

The ex-Nvidia boss' affair with Alice Huang, the former director of a Singaporean data centre firm called Megaspeed, has raised the level of scrutiny over deals abroad .

The small South East Asian business hub has been a draw for companies all around the world, many of which have set up headquarters in Singapore.

Major US firms like Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have set up offices in the business-friendly country, alongside Chinese companies like TikTok-owner ByteDance and Tencent.

But Singapore's openness to business has also made it the ideal address to place orders for restricted advanced semiconductors.

Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the chip giant earns.

But notably, only 2% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, which acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere.

While Singapore does not necessarily prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.

Advanced semiconductors, crucial for the development of AI models, are at the centre of the US and China's technological rivalry.

US officials have long viewed the country's technological supremacy as a matter of national security and have expressed concerns that sharing the best chips could give China's economy and military a boost.

Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.

Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.

The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.

Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X. , external

"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."

But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".

Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.

Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.

For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says

Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy

Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?

items.title: Tokendoctor – See what your Claude Code use overpays
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/localixai/tokendoctor Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50526584 Points: 23 # Comments: 12
items.content:
See what your Claude Code use overpays, fix it, undo it any time. Runs on your machine.

There is no one pill. If your sessions rarely pass 400K tokens, the window changes nothing for you; a summary that lands just before you finish can cost more than it saves; your models, effort and work all move the number. So tokendoctor shows you yours first: /tokendoctor:sessions replays your own sessions at smaller windows before anything changes.

/tokendoctor:dashboard : every token by day, model, effort, main thread and each subagent, context size and project. One local file; this is the author's own.

Update with claude plugin marketplace update tokendoctor and claude plugin update tokendoctor@tokendoctor , then restart Claude Code. To try it without installing, clone the repository and run claude --plugin-dir /path/to/tokendoctor .

/tokendoctor is answered by the plugin itself, so it costs nothing. Tab completes the names ( window , slide , cache , effort , model , subagents , and /tokendoctor all for the rest) and their values; /tokendoctor window 400k applies as typed, /tokendoctor window reset goes back to the default, --project or --local writes there instead of your user settings. A model name must be an alias ( opus , sonnet , haiku ) or a claude-… id.

optimize changes only settings on the tunable list and /config rows. Every change opens a dialog that shows it and runs only on Apply ; with no one to ask, as in a -p run, nothing changes. Hooks and permissions are never on the list.

The plugin's bin/ directory is on the Bash tool's PATH while it is enabled:

The skills are user-invoked only ( disable-model-invocation ). claude plugin details tokendoctor@tokendoctor estimates about 235 tokens of always-on cost for the five of them. The plugin has no MCP server. Its hooks module adds the optimize tools ( mcp__tokendoctor__* ) behind ToolSearch, so only their names are listed until /tokendoctor:optimize loads them. /tokendoctor and the slide run in the hooks module too, with no model call, so they add no tokens. Its one command hook runs tokendoctor-record in the background when a session starts. The hook is async and prints nothing, so it adds no tokens. It appends each finished day's totals to ~/.claude/tokendoctor/history.jsonl , so the trend outlives Claude Code's transcript cleanup.

Errors are settings that are wrong or ignored, warnings are likely to cost real money, and info is worth a look. Rules that depend on a Claude Code release are skipped on older versions.

templates/statusline.sh is the status line script the fix installs into your Claude config folder. templates/agents/ holds three generic subagents ( Explore , test-runner , docs-lookup ), each pinned to a small model with read-only or narrow tools. A plugin cannot override a built-in agent or ship settings.json keys such as autoCompactWindow , env or permissions , so the apply step copies the template into ~/.claude/agents/ or .claude/agents/ and edits your settings files itself, with a backup.

Claude Code changes every few days, so the audit does not trust a list frozen into the plugin:

Off by default. With /tokendoctor slide on (or tokendoctor-set tokendoctor.slide true --write , or /tokendoctor:optimize ), where Claude Code would compact, the plugin's hooks module elides old tool outputs into short pointers instead of summarizing, the way llx does. Every prompt, answer and decision stays word for word, and there is no summary pause.

In one real session, at the same size: Claude Code's summary took 367K to 35K in 65.3 s ; the slide took 368K to 36K in 0.04 s . Summaries in the author's real sessions take 79 s on average (109 of them, 22 September to 1 November).

On bench/ , Claude Code doing a TypeScript project against fixed acceptance tests, Haiku 5.5, a 100K window so that it compacts several times (medians). A short task with one compaction gains time but not money; the longer the work, the more the slide saves:

The earlier, smaller runs of node bench/window.mjs (60 files of 300 lines read one by one, then a follow-up in the same session, 200K window) cost the same both ways:

What a summary loses, measured with --task recall : the session starts with five decisions from the person, the files are deleted after reading, and the follow-up asks for the decisions and eight KEYs the model noted. Claude Code's summary kept them all: 6/6 and 8/8 in every run on both models. The slide did the same on Haiku 5.5 (3 runs, 2% dearer); on Sonnet 5.5 (1 run) it missed one KEY, which the model skipped noting in its first reply after a slide. So far no test shows the slide answering better, or worse: it saves time and money, not quality.

test/private.test.mjs fails if anything git would commit holds an API key or token, a home folder path or a temporary folder of the machine: benchmark results come from runs on someone's account, so only their summaries are committed and the transcripts stay local.

The landing page lives in site/ ( cd site && npm install && npm run dev ; npm run build prerenders it, node scripts/og.mjs redraws the social card). The demo is a real session recorded with asciinema; site/scripts/RECORDING.md says how to record it again.

Rules are pure functions over a snapshot ( lib/rules.mjs ); reading the disk lives in lib/collect.mjs and writing in lib/apply.mjs . Adding a rule means adding one entry and its test. Session analysis is in lib/sessions.mjs and lib/history.mjs , the settings tokendoctor-set may change in lib/tunables.mjs , the /tokendoctor command in lib/console.mjs , the replay in lib/replay.mjs , the slide in hooks/window.ts , and the optimize tools in hooks/register.ts .

items.title: If an App Asks for Full Disk Access or System and App Protection Override
items.summary: Article URL: https://support.apple.com/en-us/149699 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50526560 Points: 113 # Comments: 59
items.content:
Starting in macOS 27.3, when some apps ask for Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override, you have the option to choose only specific protected folders or apps for the app to access. This puts you in control of what data is accessible to the app.

Apps that might ask for Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override include backup apps, disk cleaners, file indexers, security apps, and others. While some of these apps operate best when granted broader access, others may ask for the same level of access even when they don't need it. It's important to understand the risks of granting broad access to any app, so you can make informed decisions about your own data and privacy.

When you give an app Full Disk Access instead of choosing only specific protected folders for it to access, it can bypass system protections and access all of the files on your Mac, including your messages, emails, photos and videos, data from other user accounts, and more. It can read, change, delete, and export this data without asking.

When you give an app System & App Protection Override, you can choose specific apps for it to control. If you allow it to bypass system protections instead, it can fully control your Mac and apps, which allows it to access all of your data. It can also see every window and app, including ones in the background, and capture every keystroke.

An app might ask you to give it access to all of the files on your Mac, or to let it control your Mac. When you turn on access for the app in Privacy & Security settings, depending on the app, your Mac prompts you to:

Allow or not allow the app to have access. This option appears for some apps, such as backup apps that ask for Full Disk Access, and screen readers and voice control tools that ask for Accessibility.

Choose specific protected folders or apps for the app to access instead. This option appears for other apps that ask for Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override. It allows the app to access only what you choose, while system protections stay in place for the rest of your data.

To keep more of your data protected, choose specific protected folders or apps for the app to access instead of bypassing system protections.

When your Mac prompts you, click Choose Folder or Choose Apps, then:

Check the app's setup instructions for information about which protected folders or apps it needs.

For System & App Protection Override, choose whether the app needs to ask for your permission before it controls each app. Use the menu next to each app to choose Ask First or At Any Time.

If you're not sure which protected folders or apps to choose, contact the app developer . To stay protected, wait until you're sure which folders or apps that the app needs before giving access.

You can change which protected folders or apps that the app can access at any time.

Bypassing system protections might expose your personal information to an app that doesn't behave as you expect. An app with Full Disk Access can read, change, delete, and export all of the files on your Mac, and an app with System & App Protection Override can fully control your Mac and apps.

If you're certain that the app is from a trustworthy source and needs this level of access, you can give it Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override permissions by clicking Bypass System Protections:

Full Disk Access: Read, Change, Delete, and Export All Your Data; View Hidden and Recently Deleted Photos; and Browse As You on Websites.

System & App Protection Override: Read, Change, Delete, and Export All Your Data; View Hidden and Recently Deleted Photos; Browse As You on Websites; Control Your Mac, Apps, and Settings; and Monitor Everything You Do.

If you're absolutely sure that you want to give the app Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override, click Turn On Full Disk Access or Allow System & App Protection Override, then enter your password and click Modify Settings.

You can review app permissions in Privacy & Security settings, and change or remove them at any time.

Click Privacy & Security in the sidebar, then click Files & Folders, Full Disk Access, or System & App Protection Override.

Remove an app's access: Select the app, then click the Remove button (−). If asked, enter your password, then click Modify Settings.

Change which protected folders or apps an app can access: In Files & Folders or System & App Protection Override, click the Info button (i) next to the app, make your changes, then click Done.

Limit an app with Full Disk Access or System & App Protection Override to specific protected folders or apps: Remove the app's access, then click the Add button (+) to add the app again. If your Mac prompts you, choose specific folders or apps.

If you remove an app's access, the app might not work as expected.

items.title: Mem Is Shutting Down
items.summary: Article URL: https://get.mem.ai/blog/mem-is-shutting-down Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50526537 Points: 53 # Comments: 78
items.content:
After a lot of thought, we’ve made the difficult decision to bring Mem to a close. Mem will shut down on January 15, 2027.

Over the years, you’ve trusted us with your ideas, meeting notes, unfinished drafts, and things you wanted to remember. Thank you for that trust. We know a notes app can become part of your daily life, and moving away from one takes time and care.

Our focus during these final weeks is helping you take your notes with you.

You won’t be charged again. All charging has been paused. The paid features, functionality, and limits you previously paid for will be honored for the remainder of Mem’s availability, with notes becoming read-only on December 18.

You don’t need to choose your next app right away. Start by saving a copy of your library. Our migration guide walks you through that download and moving to Apple Notes, Notion, Google Docs, Obsidian, OneNote, and other apps. It also explains what to check afterward, including attachments, collections, and meeting transcripts.

We built Mem around a question: what if your notes could do more than sit in a folder? What if they could help you remember, make connections, and use what you already knew?

From catching a thought with a keyboard shortcut to finding connections, writing with AI, and having a conversation with your knowledge, each step grew out of that same question. These moments come from our original newsletters, product walkthroughs, and launch emails, with the interfaces and demos we shared along the way.

Mem Spotlight let you create a note from anywhere on your Mac with a keyboard shortcut. Capture first, get back to what you were doing, and find the thought waiting in your Timeline later. That small interaction captured a lot of what we wanted Mem to feel like.

Search began understanding clues like dates, links, and people. You could ask for “mems that contain Twitter links from July 2021,” instead of remembering an exact title.

Mem X used embeddings to find notes by meaning and surface related ideas. Similar Mems could bring back a thought you’d forgotten, without asking you to maintain a perfect filing system.

Smart Write & Edit brought generative AI into your notes. It could help draft a message, prepare for a meeting, or develop an idea using the knowledge you had already saved.

Collections grew out of the tags people were already using. Mem suggested relevant Collections as you wrote and found notes you might have forgotten to include. You could rename, merge, and organize them in bulk as your thinking changed.

The next step was helping you notice themes you hadn’t named yet. When you wrote about something new, Mem could suggest a new Collection—not just an existing one. You could accept it, change its name, or keep writing.

With Mem Chat, your notes became something you could ask questions of. Our summer walkthrough showed how a simple question could surface a specific fact from your saved knowledge, with Smart Cards linking back to the notes behind an answer.

We rebuilt Mem around dependable, offline-first capture and recall. Voice Mode turned spoken thoughts and meetings into notes, and a new Chrome extension made saving from the web easier. The two arrows in our new logo represented you and Mem thinking together.

Mem could detect when you joined a call and offer to start taking notes with one click, without a bot joining the meeting. It also detected the end of the call, so you didn’t have to remember to stop recording.

We introduced Heads Up Live and Meeting Briefings in beta for Mem Pro. One surfaced relevant context during a recorded meeting; the other helped you prepare before a calendar-linked meeting began.

The Mem app for ChatGPT brought your saved knowledge into another place you were already thinking and working. Alongside our MCP connector, it was another way to make your notes useful beyond Mem itself.

Mem Agent arrived in iMessage, WhatsApp, email, and Slack. It connected the context in your notes with proactive follow-ups, bringing back a useful next step when it was time to act.

Behind each launch were people trying it, telling us where it fell short, and helping us make it better. The release posts record what we shipped. Your feedback shaped what those things became.

To everyone who used Mem, shared it with a friend, sent us a thoughtful bug report, or trusted us with an idea before it was fully formed: thank you.

And to the team and the people who supported us along the way, thank you for the care you put into building this product.

We’re proud of the ideas we explored together. More than anything, we want the work you put into Mem to remain useful to you wherever you go next.

items.title: Imran Khan seeks urgent medical care fearing he 'may not return alive'
items.summary: Pakistan's ex-prime minister, who has been in prison since August 2023, says he has been denied justice.
items.content:
Pakistan's jailed former PM Imran Khan has appealed for urgent medical treatment, saying that his and his wife's health has been deteriorating.

"At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive," the cricket star-turned-politician wrote in a letter published by his lawyer Salman Safdar.

Authorities in Islamabad maintain that Khan gets seen weekly by doctors, who have assessed that he is of "satisfactory" health.

Khan, who faces more than 100 charges, has been in prison since August 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Khan argues the cases against them, ranging from corruption to selling state gifts, are politically motivated.

Concerns over Khan's health have grown louder in the past year, with his family claiming he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

In his letter, Khan wrote that doctors have told him he is "highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest", and that his heart has already "suffered damage".

He also expressed concern for Bushra Bibi, whom he says suffered a detached retina in April and underwent surgery in secrecy. Khan said he fears she may lose her sight without further surgery.

"I have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and I have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice," he wrote.

He said that he is being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day, where he is allowed neither visits by his family nor access to books and television, and that this has "taken a heavy toll" on his mental health.

He also claimed he had only seen his lawyers four times over the past year.

"I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote.

Pakistan's parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry disputed these claims, saying Khan is "provided with all facilities in prison, including food of his own choosing".

"[He] is currently the most well-accommodated prisoner in Pakistan," the minister told reporters.

Authorities also say Khan was taken to a government-run hospital for an eye injection a week ago, where doctors deemed him "clinically stable".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things.

At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence.

Even behind bars, Khan remains a force in Pakistani politics.

Thousands of his supporters took to the streets in early October in a dayslong march , demanding his release. Authorities later ordered a crackdown on protests and imposed a state of emergency in Khan's party stronghold, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, insisting that Khan be given proper medical care.

items.title: Running coding agents without handing them my credentials
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.antonio.cx/running-agents-with-lend Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50526152 Points: 110 # Comments: 68
items.content:
I built lend to let remote agents use tools on my laptop with my approval. Here's how it fits into my workflow.

I use agents heavily these days as part of my toolchain. I usually have a few going at once: Claude Code working in one repo, Codex reviewing a branch in another, and something long-running in the background. I often have them review each other's work too. None of them run on my laptop. They run on VMs I can throw away, and my laptop keeps the stuff I care about: my SSH keys, my 1Password vault, and the gh and cloud CLIs that are logged in as me.

I run those agents on picd , our hosting service at pico.sh . It gives me my own VM with a Docker engine and a shell over SSH. I run herdr and the agents there, and my home directory persists across restarts so my dotfiles and tools stay in place.

This works great until an agent needs something on my laptop. In this post I'll go over how I run agents in parallel with herdr and Ovis , and the tool I wrote to deal with credentials, lend .

herdr is a terminal multiplexer built for coding agents. You get the usual workspaces, tabs, and panes, and it also knows which agent is running in each pane and what it's doing. The sidebar shows whether each agent is working, waiting on me, or done, so I can tell at a glance which one needs attention.

The CLI talks to the running session, so agents can drive each other. An agent can start Codex in another pane, give it a prompt, wait for it to finish, and read what it said:

Remote hosts work the same way. herdr machine add agent-vm sets up herdr on the VM and adds its sessions to my local client. Those sessions keep running after I disconnect.

Ovis is a browser and phone client for herdr. It shows each agent's transcript as a chat, with the live terminal a tap away. When an agent asks for approval or has a question, Ovis turns it into a card I can answer and sends me a push notification. It picks up the machines saved in herdr, so my VMs show up without any extra setup. I reach it over Tailscale.

If an agent gets stuck on a question while I'm away from my desk, I answer it from my phone and the other agents keep going.

Agents on a VM still need to act as me. I use them to monitor CI with gh , call APIs with tokens from 1Password, and SSH into other hosts. There are two usual ways to make that work, and I don't love either of them.

The first is copying credentials onto the VM. A token in ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml can be read by every process on that machine, including the agent and anything it runs, for as long as the token is valid.

The second is forwarding my SSH agent with ssh -A . The private keys stay on my laptop, but the VM can use every key in the agent without asking and without any record of what it signed. It also only covers SSH keys.

What I wanted was for the credentials to stay on the laptop and for the commands that need them to run there too. The agent asks to run something, I approve it with Touch ID, and the agent gets the output back.

That's where lend comes in. lend is a proxy that sits in front of your existing SSH agent, and you forward its socket in place of the real one. SSH and Git keep working like normal, and lend adds a way to run commands through an SSH agent extension.

When an agent on the VM asks to run gh , the request goes over the socket and gh runs on my laptop with my login. The token never leaves the laptop, so the agent never has it. Every request, whether it's a signature or a command, is checked against a policy on the laptop and needs my approval before anything happens.

The policy lives on the laptop and lists what the VM is allowed to ask for. Everything else is denied. Mine is pretty short:

A rule can also take an args_prefix like ["pr", "view"] if you only want to allow some subcommands. biometric:inline puts Touch ID right in the request dialog, so I read the request and touch once to approve it. Plain biometric asks for Touch ID in a second prompt after I click Allow.

To connect, I run lend ssh from the laptop. It starts a proxy for that one connection and stops it when SSH exits:

I run herdr on the VM. Claude Code talks to lend through lend mcp , an MCP server with a single tool called run_local_command . The tool takes the command to run and a reason, and the reason is required:

Here I asked Claude Code on the VM for the lend repo's description. It called the tool with gh repo view , my Mac showed the request, and one touch approved it:

The dialog shows the full path to the executable, every argument, the directory it'll run in on the laptop, the reason, and what the remote process said about itself. Once I approve, gh runs on the laptop and stdout, stderr, and the exit code stream back to the agent. The reason and caller details come from the VM, so they're marked as unverified. They're there to help me decide and can't change what the policy allows.

If you'd rather skip MCP, the same request works as a plain CLI call on the VM:

herdr panes survive an SSH disconnect, but the forwarded socket belongs to that connection. When I reconnect, SSH gives me a new socket path. Agents still running in the panes keep the old SSH_AUTH_SOCK .

I use a symlink at a fixed path and update it from ~/.ssh/rc on the VM. SSH runs this before starting the shell, so it sees the socket forwarded by the new connection:

New Bash shells in herdr panes pick up the stable path when it works. If the check fails, Bash leaves SSH_AUTH_SOCK alone. MCP, approval hooks, and Git inherit that path when I start them. After reconnecting, the SSH hook updates the symlink and those processes use the new socket for subsequent requests. Agents already running with an old socket path need to be restarted once with the stable path in their environment.

The SSH connection from the laptop still has to stay open. Requests fail while it's disconnected, and reconnecting starts a new lend session with fresh approvals and leases. The link points at one connection at a time, so the last update wins.

gh works because it's already logged in on my laptop. Some tools need a token passed in. For those, a command rule can read secrets with something like op read and hand them to the approved command as environment variables:

When the agent asks to run gh pr view and I approve it, lend reads the token from 1Password, runs gh with GH_TOKEN set, and sends back the output. The token stays on the laptop. The VM can't pick which variables get set or which references get read. The prompt shows the variable names and references, and the values never show up in prompts or history.

Here's the VM running gh api user with a rule that injects GH_TOKEN . After I approve in lend, 1Password asks for its own Touch ID before op read returns the token. The VM gets my login back, and its own environment has no GH_TOKEN :

There's one catch: this only works if the approved command doesn't print its environment. If you approve env or sh , you've handed the values right back. The same goes for allowing op itself as a command, since op read prints the secret and that output goes straight to the agent.

Keys get their own policy too. Keys that aren't listed are hidden from the VM, and listed keys can be limited by what they're allowed to sign. max_signatures caps how many signatures a key can make in a session.

A rule can offer a lease when I approve, like five minutes or three uses. Leases only exist inside a lend ssh session and only match the exact command and arguments I approved. They go away when the session ends or my screen locks.

lend status --all --watch shows what's connected, what's waiting, what's running, and any active leases. lend pause --all cancels everything and refuses new requests until I resume. lend history keeps a record of what ran and how it was approved. It leaves out arguments, output, and secrets, and you can opt into logging arguments.

Agents also ask permission for things that have nothing to do with my credentials, like running a shell command on the VM, editing a file, or fetching a URL. lend approve sends those questions to the same dialog on my Mac. It doesn't run anything on the laptop. It asks me, and the agent decides what to do with the answer.

Now when Claude Code would normally stop and ask in the terminal, my Mac shows the command or tool input and I answer with Touch ID. The laptop policy lists which topics are allowed to ask, each with its own approval:

There are adapters for Codex, Antigravity, and pi, plus a plain JSON format for anything else. You can use it in scripts too: lend approve --topic deploy --title "terraform apply" && terraform apply only applies after I approve on the laptop. If the laptop can't be reached, the hook stays out of the way and the agent asks in its own UI like it normally would.

An approved command runs as my user and can touch my files. Approval decides what runs, and lend doesn't sandbox it. If I approve a shell, an interpreter, or anything that reads instructions from stdin, I've basically approved running anything on my laptop, since stdin streams after approval and isn't shown in the prompt.

items.title: Narwal Flow 2 e Freo 20 Edge a confronto. Cosa cambia nella pulizia di tutti i giorni
items.summary: Hanno tante caratteristiche in comune ma anche importanti differenze. Come scegliere? Ecco una guida completa ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Scegliere tra Narwal Flow 2 e Freo 20 Edge guardando soltanto la potenza di aspirazione sarebbe quasi impossibile: entrambi arrivano a 31.000 Pa. Anche sul lavaggio condividono uno degli elementi più caratteristici della nuova generazione Narwal, il Track Mop, cioè un mocio a rullo piatto che viene continuamente pulito mentre passa sul pavimento.

Flow 2 è il modello flagship: punta a ridurre il più possibile gli interventi dell'utente e aggiunge un sistema di navigazione più sofisticato, riconoscimento dello sporco, gestione evoluta dei tappeti, maggiore capacità di superare gli ostacoli e una stazione più completa.

Freo 20 Edge invece parte da un'altra idea: conservare alcune delle tecnologie che distinguono i modelli di fascia superiore, a cominciare proprio da FlowWash e dal Track Mop, portandole a un livello di prezzo più accessibile.

Non è quindi soltanto una questione di "modello migliore" e "modello peggiore". E anche il prezzo potrebbe ingannare: non per forza il Flow 2, di fascia superiore, è più adatto rispetto al Freo 20 Edge per la propria esigenza.

La risposta dipende soprattutto dal tipo di casa, dalla pulizia quotidiana che viene effettuata e anche dal grado di automazione che si preferisce.

In entrambi i casi il momento è ghiotto: per il Black Friday sono scontati su Amazon e sullo store online di Narwal . Flow 2 costa 899 euro anziché 1.299 euro. Mentre il Freo 20 Edge è scontato a 489 euro anziché 799 euro. Gli sconti sono validi anche sul sito ufficiale di Narwal.

Inoltre, sui due modelli usando il codice sconto NBFDDAY26 si ottiene un ulteriore 5% di sconto, sia su Amazon sia sul sito ufficiale Narwal . Così il Flow 2 scende a 854,05 euro, mentre il Freo 20 Edge scende a 464,55 euro.

Il codice sconto va inserito in fase di checkout nel campo “Aggiungi un buono regalo, un codice promozionale o un coupon”. Una volta inserito il codice basta confermarlo cliccando sulla freccia e assicurarsi che venga inserito come saldo promozionale.

La tecnologia più importante che accomuna Flow 2 e Freo 20 Edge è il sistema FlowWash con Track Mop. A differenza dei robot che utilizzano due panni circolari rotanti, Narwal impiega un elemento a rullo piatto che viene risciacquato durante la pulizia . In questo modo si evita che il robot continui a trascinare da una zona all'altra lo sporco raccolto poco prima.

Entrambi i modelli applicano sul pavimento una pressione di 12 N, possono estendere lateralmente il Track Mop per raggiungere meglio i bordi e lo sollevano di 12 mm quando necessario. Identica anche la capacità del serbatoio dell'acqua pulita: 130 ml per entrambi i modelli.

La differenza fra i due modelli riguarda il modo in cui viene gestito il Track Mop. Su Flow 2 il rullo viene risciacquato durante la pulizia con acqua calda fino a 60 °C . Serve soprattutto ad affrontare sporco più ostinato, come residui grassi, caffè secco o impronte lasciate sul pavimento.

Freo 20 Edge mantiene invece il Track Mop autopulente, ma senza il lavaggio ad acqua calda durante il passaggio.

L’aspirazione è l’elemento che, almeno sulla carta, più accomuna i due modelli: Flow 2 e Freo 20 Edge raggiungono entrambi una potenza massima di 31.000 Pa.

Condividono anche la spazzola principale flottante anti-groviglio e la spazzola laterale anti-groviglio, pensate per accompagnare capelli e peli verso il canale di aspirazione riducendo la quantità di materiale che rimane avvolto attorno agli elementi rotanti. Il contenitore della polvere integrato nel robot è in entrambi i casi da 300 ml .

Ci sono però alcuni dettagli importanti da considerare. Flow 2 aggiunge CarpetFocus, assente sul Freo 20 Edge . È il sistema pensato per aumentare l'efficacia della pulizia sui tappeti, una differenza che acquista peso nelle abitazioni in cui le superfici tessili occupano una parte importante degli ambienti. E proprio la combinazione tra aspirazione, spazzole anti-groviglio e gestione del lavaggio rende Flow 2 particolarmente interessante nelle case con animali.

A questi elementi si aggiunge Pet Care Mode 2.0, che permette al robot di adattare maggiormente il proprio comportamento agli ambienti nei quali vivono animali domestici . In pratica, riduce la rumorosità e la potenza in modo da proseguire le attività di pulizia ma non disturbare gli animali.

Il Flow 2 include anche la funzione “Trova il tuo animale” per interagire a distanza, anche con la voce, con i propri animali domestici. Lo stesso avviene con i bambini piccoli: la modalità Baby Care serve a riconoscere le aree dedicati ai più piccoli e a ridurre il rumore, pur mantenendo standard di pulizia elevati.

Così come il Flow 2, il più accessibile Freo 20 Edge può raggiungere il più possibile lo sporco che tende a rimanere lungo il perimetro delle stanze. Il sistema EdgeReach permette, infatti, di estendere il Track Mop verso l'esterno , in modo da lavorare più vicino ai battiscopa e raggiungere gli angoli a 90 gradi. In più, è davvero silenzioso: lavora a 55,8 dB.

Una delle distanze maggiori tra i due modelli emerge nella navigazione. Entrambi utilizzano un sensore LiDAR integrato nella scocca, soluzione che permette di mantenere l'altezza del robot a 95 mm. Cambia però il sistema utilizzato per osservare ciò che si trova davanti al robot.

Flow 2 abbina due telecamere RGB alla luce strutturata laterale e può riconoscere una gamma aperta di oggetti. È anche in grado di individuare intelligentemente lo sporco, distinguendo tra residui secchi da aspirare e macchie umide da lavare.

Dall’altra parte, Freo 20 Edge rinuncia alle telecamere e utilizza luce strutturata sui due lati. Può riconoscere oltre 150 tipologie di oggetti, ma non dispone del rilevamento intelligente delle macchie. Il risultato è che Flow 2 può adattare maggiormente la pulizia a ciò che trova davanti a sé, mentre Freo 20 Edge adotta un approccio più essenziale.

C'è una differenza anche nel superamento delle soglie: Flow 2 può affrontare dislivelli fino a 3 cm nel caso di un singolo gradino e fino a 4 cm con una configurazione a doppio gradino. Freo 20 Edge arriva invece a 2 cm.

In una casa su un unico livello con pavimenti uniformi può cambiare poco. Se ci sono soglie marcate tra le stanze, binari o piccoli dislivelli, il margine aggiuntivo del Flow 2 diventa invece più significativo.

Flow 2 utilizza Freo Mind 4.0 e aggiunge un assistente vocale basato sull'Intelligenza Artificiale. Inoltre è compatibile con dispositivi che supportano Siri, Google Home e Alexa e permette anche di utilizzare la videocamera per le videochiamate.

Freo 20 Edge dispone invece di Freo Mind e mantiene il controllo attraverso gli ecosistemi vocali esterni, ma non include né l'assistente IA integrato né la funzione di videochiamata. Sono caratteristiche che non incidono direttamente sulla capacità di aspirare una briciola o lavare una macchia, ma diventano rilevanti se l'obiettivo è avere un dispositivo che partecipi più attivamente all'ecosistema della casa.

Per semplificare, Flow 2 è il modello che cerca di comprendere maggiormente l'ambiente; Freo 20 Edge punta a svolgere in maniera automatica e prevedibile le operazioni principali.

C’è una differenza importante anche sull’autonomia. Flow 2 integra una batteria da 7.000 mAh, mentre quella di Freo 20 Edge è da 5.200 mAh. Si tratta di una scelta consapevole da parte di Narwal: Flow 2 è pensato anche per abitazioni medio-grandi da 120-200 metri quadrati e, quindi, deve gestire sessioni più lunghe; mentre Freo 20 Edge è indirizzato soprattutto ad appartamenti e case di piccole o medie dimensioni.

Significa che Freo 20 Edge rischia di rimanere bloccato a metà pulizia? No, perché il sistema intelligente fa sì che il robot sia autonomo anche in questo: può gestire il proprio ciclo tornando alla stazione quando necessario. La maggiore capacità del Flow 2, però, riduce la necessità di interrompere una sessione nelle abitazioni più estese.

Se i due robot condividono diverse tecnologie sul pavimento, è nella base che Flow 2 prende più nettamente le distanze. Entrambi possono accumulare la polvere per periodi prolungati : Flow 2 utilizza un sacchetto da 2,4 litri e Freo 20 Edge uno da 2,5 litri, con un'autonomia fino a 120 giorni prima della sostituzione.

I serbatoi dell'acqua di Flow 2 sono da 4,5 litri per quella pulita e 4 litri per quella sporca; gli stessi valori vengono utilizzati dal Freo 20 Edge.

La stazione di Flow 2 può lavare il Track Mop con acqua calda regolata dinamicamente tra 45 e 100 °C e utilizza aria a 60 °C per l'asciugatura. È presente anche il dosaggio automatico del detergente.

Freo 20 Edge, invece, asciuga il Track Mop con aria a 45 °C e non dispone né del lavaggio del mocio con acqua calda nella stazione né del dosaggio automatico del detergente.

Come tradurre questi numeri e queste caratteristiche tecniche in una scelta personale? Facciamo degli esempi pratici. Pensiamo a una casa con pavimenti misti, un cane che entra dal giardino e un tappeto nel punto in cui si riposa. In una stessa sessione il robot deve raccogliere peli, affrontare impronte e passare dal pavimento duro al tappeto. In questo caso Flow 2 permette di usare con regolarità le funzioni per cui si paga la differenza di prezzo.

items.title: Black Friday UGREEN, sei idee regalo tra NAS e accessori con sconti fino al 30%
items.summary: NAS per tenere in casa foto e documenti di famiglia, un power bank magnetico, un caricatore da scrivania da 300 W e un dock Thunderbolt 5. Con gli sconti già attivi su Amazon e sullo store UGREEN i regali di Natale si sistemano in anticipo ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
UGREEN anticipa il Black Friday e sconta già NAS, power bank, caricatori e docking station su Amazon e sul suo negozio online , con riduzioni di prezzo che arrivano fino al 30% rispetto al listino .

Gli sconti giungono a poco più di un mese da Natale e tornano utili a chi vuole sistemare in anticipo i regali tecnologici, o a chi vuole farseli. La selezione comprende sei prodotti. Tre sono NAS della serie NASync, gli altri tre sono accessori per chi lavora con un portatile e uno smartphone da tenere sempre carichi.

Il DH2300 ha due alloggiamenti per dischi SATA, fino a 64 TB in tutto. Con il RAID 1 scrive ogni file su entrambi i dischi, così se uno si guasta l'archivio resta intatto sull'altro .

Lo muove un processore Rockchip ARM a 8 core con 4 GB di memoria. La porta di rete è una 1GbE, e c'è un'uscita HDMI 4K a 60 Hz .

Affinché il NAS sia davvero utile su tutti i dispositivi, l'app di gestione funziona su Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, nel browser e sulle smart TV.

Nella libreria fotografica il NAS riconosce volti, scene e luoghi, elimina i duplicati e crea album; per condividere una raccolta con i parenti si manda semplicemente un link o un QR code .

Il listino è di 246,99 euro e in offerta il prezzo scende a 199,99 euro, il 19% in meno. Il DH2300 si compra su Amazon oppure sullo store ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP2800 GT mantiene due alloggiamenti per hard disk ma aggiunge due slot per SSD M.2 NVMe , per una capienza massima di 80 TB . Il processore è un AMD Ryzen Embedded R2514 a 4 core e 8 thread, fino a 3,7 GHz, con 8 GB di memoria DDR4 espandibili fino a 64 GB.

La differenza principale rispetto al DH2300 sta nella porta di rete da 10GbE , che in teoria trasferisce fino a 1,25 GB al secondo, quattro volte una porta 2,5GbE.

Il sistema supporta Docker, le macchine virtuali e un centro di videosorveglianza, e l'accesso da fuori casa passa dal servizio UGREENlink, incluso.

Dal listino di 509,99 euro si passa a 429,99 euro, con uno sconto del 16%. Lo si trova nella pagina Amazon del prodotto e sul sito di UGREEN .

Con quattro alloggiamenti per hard disk e due slot M.2 da usare come cache, il DXP4800 Pro arriva a 144 TB . Oltre al RAID 1 supporta anche il RAID 5 e il RAID 6 , che distribuiscono su tutti i dischi informazioni di controllo con cui ricostruire i dati se se ne rompe uno, o due nel caso del RAID 6.

Dentro c'è un Intel Core i3-1315U di tredicesima generazione, 6 core e 8 thread, con 8 GB di memoria DDR5 espandibili fino a 96 GB, mentre il sistema operativo gira su un SSD dedicato da 128 GB .

Le porte di rete sono due, una 2,5GbE e una 10GbE , e c'è un lettore di schede SD per scaricare le foto della fotocamera direttamente sul NAS. Come il DXP2800 GT supporta Docker e le macchine virtuali.

Il prezzo di listino di 799,99 euro scende a 679,99 euro, il 15% in meno. Chi lo vuole ordinare può farlo da Amazon o dallo store UGREEN .

Il MagFlow Pro ha una batteria da 10.000 mAh e pesa 230 grammi. Si aggancia magneticamente al retro dello smartphone e lo ricarica senza fili con lo standard Qi2 a 25 W, mentre il cavo USB-C integrato eroga fino a 45 W a un secondo dispositivo , che può essere ricaricato insieme al primo.

Sul corpo c'è anche un display . Per contenere le temperature UGREEN ha utilizzato un sistema di raffreddamento a liquido.

Costa 129,99 euro di listino e 115,99 euro in offerta, con uno sconto dell'11%. È in vendita sullo store UGREEN .

Il caricatore da scrivania Nexode Pro ha otto porte e una potenza complessiva di 300 W , con un massimo di 140 W su una singola porta USB-C. Usa chip al nitruro di gallio (GaN). È in grado di portare due MacBook Pro al 50% in 28 minuti.

Toccando la parte superiore si passa tra cinque modalità di ricarica , che si possono cambiare anche dall'app, insieme al controllo dello stato delle porte.

Dal listino di 169,99 euro il prezzo scende a 125,99 euro usando il 25% in meno. Si ordina dal negozio online di UGREEN e lo sconto si applica usando il codice sconto presente sulla pagina.

Il Revodok Max 2131 , una dock 13 in 1 che si collega a un portatile Thunderbolt 5 o Thunderbolt 4 e mette a disposizione tre porte Thunderbolt 5 a valle, una USB-C, quattro USB-A, una porta Ethernet 2,5GbE, un lettore di schede SD e microSD UHS-II e un jack audio . Con lo stesso cavo ricarica il computer fino a 140 W , grazie all'alimentatore da 180 W incluso.

Ha una banda fino a 120 Gb/s. Ai monitor dedica le porte Thunderbolt 5, con cui gestisce un monitor 8K a 60 Hz, due monitor 6K a 60 Hz oppure tre monitor 4K a 144 Hz .

Su un listino di 429,99 euro, in offerta costa 300,99 euro. Con il 30% in meno è lo sconto più alto della selezione , e anche in questo caso l'acquisto passa dallo store ufficiale e dal codice da applicare alla chiusura dell'ordine.

Tutte le offerte UGREEN su Amazon sono raccolte nella pagina dedicata al Black Friday , con una sezione riservata ai NAS NASync ; sullo store del produttore c'è la pagina del Black Friday UGREEN .

items.title: iRobot taglia i prezzi dei Roomba: con il Black Friday si risparmiano fino a 200 euro
items.summary: Dal 16 al 30 novembre su irobot.it nove Roomba costano meno, dai compatti che lavano i pavimenti ai Max con la base che fa quasi tutto da sola ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Oggi parte il Black Friday di iRobot, che fino al 30 novembre mette in offerta nove Roomba sul negozio online irobot.it. Il pezzo più atteso è il top di gamma: il Roomba Max 875 Combo con base AutoWash che ottiene uno sconto di ben 200 euro rispetto al prezzo degli ultimi 30 giorni. All'altro capo del listino il Roomba 115 Combo scende a soli 149 euro, e in mezzo c'è un robot per ogni casa e per ogni budget. La spedizione è gratuita e c'è sempre il reso entro 30 giorni.

I modelli sono tanti, ma si "leggono" bene se li si guarda per serie. Inoltre, salendo di prezzo e di caratteristiche il robot si prende in carico sempre più lavoro, fino a lasciarci soltanto il compito di cambiare un sacchetto una volta ogni pochi mesi.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo , cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con un sensore laser LiDAR che disegna la mappa della casa, così il robot pulisce per file ordinate, sa dove è già passato e dall'app Roomba Home si scelgono le stanze da pulire.

A fare la differenza, salendo di prezzo, è soprattutto la base di ricarica. La AutoEmpty aspira lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto che si cambia ogni tre mesi circa. La AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

L'ultimo numero da tenere d'occhio è la potenza di aspirazione, misurata in pascal (Pa): indica la depressione creata dal motore, e più è alta più sporco il robot tira su da tappeti e fughe.

Nel Roomba Max 875 Combo + AutoWash iRobot ha messo il massimo della tecnologia . Per il Black Friday costa 799 euro, contro un listino di 1.199 euro. È disponibile nero o bianco.

Aspira con 35.000 Pa, il valore più alto di tutta l'offerta. Quando sale su un tappeto, la tecnologia SealForce abbassa da sola il modulo di aspirazione e rende la pulizia del tappeto fino a tre volte più efficace. Il rullo e la spazzola laterale sono anti-groviglio, pensati per chi convive con capelli lunghi e peli di cani e gatti.

Per lavare usa il rullo PowerSpin Max , che gira a 300 giri al minuto e preme sul pavimento con 18 newton.

Sulle macchie più ostinate il robot passa prima con ThermaMist , una nebbia a ultrasuoni di acqua scaldata a 60 °C che pretratta lo sporco secco.

Con PerfectEdge il rullo si allunga lateralmente di 45 mm per arrivare fino al battiscopa, mentre DriLift lo solleva quando il robot riconosce un tappeto, che così resta asciutto.

La navigazione unisce il LiDAR ClearView Pro a PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi e scarpe, e li aggira invece di trascinarli . Il robot è alto 9,98 cm, quindi passa sotto molti divani, e supera soglie fino a 3,5 cm .

La base AutoWash chiude il cerchio. Lava il rullo con acqua a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C perché non resti umido, dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere dal robot . Prima di doverla toccare passano fino a 90 giorni.

Chi vuole un Max spendendo 200 euro in meno trova il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash a 599 euro, 100 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni, nei colori nero o bianco.

Rispetto all'875 rinuncia a poco , e conserva tutte le carte della serie Max: 30.000 Pa, due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect per riconoscere le zone più sporche e Carpet Boost, che alza la potenza sui tappeti.

Lava con il rullo PowerSpin , protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti quando il robot li attraversa, e vede gli ostacoli con la stessa PrecisionVision AI dell'875. La sua base lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C e svuota la polvere fino a tre mesi .

Per le case con molti tappeti, dove il lavaggio non serve, c'è il Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , un aspirapolvere puro con gli stessi 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost del 775. La base AutoEmpty lo svuota per un massimo di 90 giorni . Durante il Black Friday costa 379 euro.

Il rullo PowerSpin scende di prezzo con la serie Plus 600, che lo usa con acqua a 60 °C e 15 newton di pressione. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, riconoscono gli ostacoli con PrecisionVision AI e sono alti 9,95 cm.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo con base Wash Only ha lo sconto più forte di tutta la campagna in percentuale, circa il 27%: costa 399 euro, 150 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni. È la strada più economica per avere il rullo lavapavimenti. La base lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga , ma non svuota la polvere , che comunque finisce in un sacchetto da un litro dentro il robot e basta per circa un mese .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash costa 549 euro, nero o bianco, e la differenza con il 615 sta tutta nella base. Questa svuota anche la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa il detergente, per arrivare fino a 90 giorni senza interventi . Sul robot c'è PerfectEdge, già visto sull'875, e una spazzola con un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira; in questo non resta avvolta e non c'è da liberarla con le forbici.

La serie Plus 400 e 500 è quella che entra dove gli altri restano fuori. Il 415 e il 575 sono alti appena 8,35 cm (il 21% in meno del Roomba Plus 505 della generazione precedente), e passano sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata. Lavano con due panni rotanti DualClean da 200 giri al minuto, che si sollevano di 10 mm quando il robot riconosce un tappeto . Entrambi hanno la base AutoWash e sono disponibili in nero o bianco.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash scende a 299 euro. Aspira con 20.000 Pa e con SmartScrub preme di più sul pavimento per staccare le macchie secche. La base lava e asciuga i panni con aria calda, così non restano umidi fino al giro successivo .

Il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash è l'occasione della fascia media: per il periodo promo costa 379 euro. Aspira con 25.000 Pa e porta su un robot così sottile la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, la stessa dei Max. La base lava i panni con acqua fino a 75 °C e poi li asciuga con aria calda.

Per cominciare a delegare la pulizia di casa basta il Roomba 115 Combo , che durante il Black Friday costa solo 149 euro, nero o bianco.

Ha la stessa navigazione laser dei modelli superiori , aspira con 15.000 Pa e lava con un panno in microfibra che si stacca e si lava.

È alto 9,2 cm e con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Con 30 euro in più si smette anche di svuotarlo. Infatti, il Roomba 115 Combo + AutoEmpty costa 179 euro, ed è il modo più economico per avere un robot che si svuota da solo. La base raccoglie lo sporco in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e dura circa tre mesi .

items.title: Kidnap, child marriage and poverty: Why millions of Nigerian children can't go to school
items.summary: BBC World Service launches programme in Hausa for out-of-school children in West Africa.
items.content:
As she pounds millet, 15-year-old Hadiza sings the English alphabet. It is a reminder of something that she desperately misses - going to school.

"Sometimes I write on the ground to practise and see if I'm still writing correctly," she says.

One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village.

"They scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We had to run away. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says.

Since then she has lived in a displaced persons camp in Goronyo, a few kilometres from her home. For a short while she went to school here, but soon met a young man and, at the age of 13, stopped going to classes and got married.

"It's tradition here that once a girl is married, her education ends," she explains.

Now she lives with her in-laws and helps look after the home.

Although Nigerian law prohibits marriage under the age of 18, it is not always enforced.

Hadiza is one of nearly 19 million children in Nigeria who are missing out on an education, according to estimates shared by Unesco in 2024. That's about one in four of the country's school-age children.

Against this backdrop, the BBC World Service has launched Dars Hausa, an educational programme in the main language spoken in northern Nigeria, as well as neighbouring Niger, Cameroon and elsewhere in West Africa.

It brings English, maths and science lessons to children across West Africa, via social media, local television partnerships and radio. Many people in the region get their news from the radio and nearly half of households in Nigeria have one, according to the charity Save the Children.

Dars means "lesson" in Pashto and Dari, and it was first launched in those languages in 2023 for Afghan children barred from attending school. An Arabic version followed in February 2025.

The reasons why so many Nigerian children are out of school are numerous and complex. Like Hadiza, 12-year-old Rukayya also lives in the displacement camp in Goronyo.

"It pains me to see other children studying and going to school while I cannot," she says.

As the eldest child, each day Rukayya goes out to gather firewood to sell and to beg so that her younger siblings can have something to eat.

"If my father was alive, I wouldn't have to go out and beg," she explains, saying some people mock her "but it doesn't stop me because it is our only way to survive."

Bandits killed her father about a year ago in front of her, she says, and her family fled from their home to the camp.

She and Hadiza are among 670,000 people in north-west and central Nigeria who have been forced from their homes by armed robbery and kidnappings, according to the International Organization for Migration.

Three Girls: Lessons in Limbo features the stories of Hadiza and Rukayya - you can watch the full film on YouTube , external

Some attacks have been carried out by militant Islamist groups, but the majority in this region are by criminal gangs, known in Nigeria as bandits, who steal, kill and kidnap.

The school that Hadiza once attended in Goronyo is the only one serving children in the camp and typically has about 50 students in each class.

One of the teachers, Kamilu Sulaiman Jakada, says that even though lessons are free, only a tiny portion of the children attend, and even then sporadically, because parents tell him that "it is the children that are the breadwinners" and they need to earn money to eat.

He says the school does not have enough teachers or classrooms, explaining that funding is inconsistent and often comes from individuals or organisations rather than the government.

The other challenge is the bandits. A gang once came to the school on motorbikes, shooting in the air, he says, and although no-one was hurt, many parents were scared and withdrew their children. That has been parents' reaction to attacks in some other parts of the country too.

Every Nigerian child is meant to get nine years of free, compulsory education - six in primary and three in secondary school. Responsibility is shared between federal, state and local governments.

But many schools are facing shortages and poorer families who cannot afford private education can struggle to pay for uniforms, books and transport.

The crisis has built up over decades, with successive governments struggling to address chronic underfunding and poor oversight of resources.

In addition, many children in the traditional Almajiri system, which provides Islamic education, are not taught subjects such as maths and science, and are considered by Unicef to be out of school.

Minister of State for Education Prof Suwaiba Sa'id believes the number of children out of school is lower than has been reported, but admits that with Nigeria's growing population "the proper investment, the proper oversight, has not been done… I will not mention the names, but we know of two states that did not recruit a single teacher for eight years".

She says that education is the government's "number-one priority" and initiatives such as Lumina are designed to help address "decades of neglect". Lumina aims to support one million girls by 2030, providing an accelerated learning programme for older girls who have missed years of formal education.

She also says that "the government is doing everything possible" to deal with bandits and that "we have seen children that should be at school but are engaged in this banditry".

In the meantime, it is children like Hadiza and Rukayya that the BBC World Service Dars Hausa programmes aim to help. Hadiza says she still has a dream to one day become a doctor "to help my fellow women".

Dars Hausa will air on BBC News Hausa radio on Sundays at 06:45 West Africa Time, with a repeat at 20:45. The programme will also be available via BBC News Hausa's digital platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram.

items.title: Il conflitto del parlamentare Angelucci: in commissione voterà sulla sanità privata
items.summary: Il deputato leghista, ras delle cliniche, passa alle Attività produttive, dove discuterà anche norme per limitare l’accesso al settore
items.content:
Il deputato della Lega Antonio Angelucci , editore dei giornali di centrodestra e proprietario delle cliniche private del centro e sud Italia, nei prossimi giorni potrebbe ritrovarsi a votare alcuni emendamenti che riguardano proprio i colossi del settore della sanità privata. Da giovedì scorso, infatti, Angelucci è nuovo membro della commissione Attività Produttive della Camera, il luogo dove viene discusso e votato il disegno di legge sulla Concorrenza che contiene anche proposte di maggioranza per limitare l’accesso al settore dei nuovi operatori della sanità privata favorendo lo status quo.

Angelucci è entrato a far parte della commissione Attività Produttive di Montecitorio giovedì scorso in un giro di spostamenti che ha riguardato diversi deputati leghisti. Tutto è partito dal trasferimento del deputato leghista Giulio Centemero che è stato indicato dal governo come nuovo membro del consiglio di amministrazione della Consob: in attesa della conferma parlamentare, Centemero ha chiesto di passare, per una questione di opportunità, dalla commissione Finanze a quella delle Politiche Europee sostituendo Angelucci.

Al posto di Centemero è andato il salviniano Luca Toccalini , fedelissimo del segretario, che ha lasciato il posto ad Angelucci. Quest’ultimo, quindi, dal 12 novembre farà parte della commissione Attività Produttive, il luogo in cui dalla prossima settimana si inizierà a votare il disegno di legge Concorrenza, provvedimento che ogni anno il governo deve presentare per promuovere la concorrenza e rimuovere ostacoli burocratici e amministrativi. Spesso, però, negli anni, si è trasformato in una legge che limita la concorrenza.

Come raccontato da Domani , Forza Italia e Fratelli d’Italia hanno presentato due emendamenti identici per limitare le gare all’interno della sanità privata con l’effetto di rendere più difficile l’accesso nel mercato di nuovi concorrenti: i bandi di gara per i servizi da garantire non inciderebbero sui contratti già in essere per le società accreditate al sistema sanitario. Per queste ultime scatterebbe il rinnovo automatico. Una norma che non può che piacere alle aziende del settore, tra cui il gruppo San Raffaele di Angelucci. Proposta contestata dai sindacati: Cgil, Cisl e Uil ne hanno chiesto il ritiro.

Angelucci, dunque, potenzialmente, si troverà a discutere e votare emendamenti che riguardano anche i suoi affari. Non è detto, tuttavia, che lo farà perché dalla Lega fanno sapere che lo spostamento è frutto del fatto che Angelucci non partecipa mai o quasi mai ai lavori delle sue commissioni e quindi è uno dei deputati che le cambia di più. Dall’inizio della legislatura, infatti, ne ha cambiate ben cinque. Inoltre, secondo i dati della Camera aggiornati a settembre scorso, Angelucci risulta essere uno dei deputati col maggior tasso di assenze: secondo le tabelle fornite da Montecitorio, il deputato leghista non ha partecipato al 99,43% delle votazioni in aula dall’inizio della legislatura, di cui il 72,6% giustificato dal partito. Angelucci si fa vedere a Montecitorio solo in occasione di votazioni molto importanti, ma non è escluso che possa tornare in commissione nei prossimi giorni.
